fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflective delineators to make it clearly visible at night or in low visibility conditions.
• Clear overhanging branches along the driveway to maintain a full-height clearance for fire and rescue apparatus.
• Trim dense vegetation along the driveway edges to keep sight lines open for approaching responders.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the residence large enough for a fire engine or ambulance to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark the turnaround area clearly so responders can identify it on arrival.
• Keep the detached structure clearly labeled or numbered if it could be confused with the main residence during an emergency response.
• Post the property address at a second location near the main residence, visible from the driveway approach.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of vehicles, equipment, or debris that would block a single-lane approach.
• Trim vegetation around the detached structure to keep all sides accessible to responders on foot.
• Keep any perimeter gates along the driveway unlocked or equipped with a Knox Box or responder-accessible lock.
• Identify and mark a secondary foot-access route across the open terrain in case the driveway becomes blocked.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation; Grass Cover; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Open Terrain; Vegetation Near Structure; Single Access Route; Long Driveway; Scattered Trees; Brush Area
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the house and any other structures on the property.
• Thin trees in clusters close to the house so there is open space between individual trees and between trees and the structure.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Clear brush from both sides of the driveway along its full length to keep the travel lane open and visible.
• Trim overhanging branches above the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Mow or cut grass growing close to the house down to a short, low height.
• Separate shrubs from nearby trees by removing or trimming vegetation that connects ground-level plants to tree canopies.
• Thin mixed vegetation surrounding the house to create open gaps and reduce the amount of plant material immediately around the structure.
• Clear brush and shrubs from the area around any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Keep the area at the driveway entrance clear and easy to identify from the main road since there is only one way in and out.
• Remove dead or dry grass and plant material from around the base of trees near the house.
• Maintain a clear turning or pull-out area near the house so emergency vehicles can maneuver without backing the full length of the driveway.
